page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU metrics generally align with average tier expectations. Memory subsystem performance shows average read and write bandwidths, though the Passmark memory score and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the lower 25% tier. Cryptographic and vector operations are supported via hardware-accelerated instructions including AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and AVX.

Given its compute-heavy resource allocation of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for CPU-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The lack of local storage and GPU accelerators makes it less suitable for heavy database storage or deep learning training. It is best suited for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, lightweight text and image processing, and basic single-threaded or moderately multi-threaded compute tasks.
